questions.question: Which description fits the **Measure** resource?
options: This resource provides the definition of a quality measure.
A structured set of tests against a FHIR server or client implementation to determine compliance against the FHIR specification.
A summary of information based on the results of executing a TestScript.
This resource contains the results of the calculation of a measure; and optionally a reference to the resources involved in that calculation.
questions.explanation: **Measure**: The Measure resource provides the definition of a quality measure. The other descriptions belong to **TestScript**, **TestReport**, **MeasureReport**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? Define a quality measure: the percentage of diabetic patients with an annual eye exam.
questions.explanation: **Measure**. The measure definition. Calculated results go in MeasureReport.

questions.question: You know **Measure**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “the logic the measure uses”?
questions.explanation: **Library**: the logic the measure uses. **Measure** is for something else: The Measure resource provides the definition of a quality measure.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **Measure** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of Measure are `status` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **Measure** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of Measure: `status`. `status`: draft | active | retired | unknown. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
